0.0.n: Connects this explanation to what came before.

0.2.n: Introduces the first point in the explanation.

0.3.n: Combines with つ and 目 to form 1つ目, meaning first.

0.4.n: A general counting suffix; 1つ counts one thing.

0.5.n: Added after a count to show position in a sequence.

0.6.n: Links 1つ目 to 機能, identifying the feature as the first one.

0.8.n: Marks the first feature as what the speaker is identifying.

0.9.n: An English loanword for a support that holds a device upright.

0.10.n: Links スタンド to 機能 to describe what kind of function it is.

0.11.n: Refers specifically to the device serving as a stand.

0.12.n: Politely finishes the identification of the first feature.

0.13.n: Softens the explanation and invites the listener to follow along.

1.0.n: Describes the following noun, pointing to the demonstrated way of using the stand.

1.1.n: In こんな感じ, it refers to how the demonstrated action looks.

1.2.n: Marks こんな感じ as the manner in which the action is done.

1.3.n: The て-form of 引き出す connects pulling the stand out with using it.

1.4.n: The plain form comes before こと to describe an action as a thing.

1.5.n: Turns 使う into a noun-like phrase so で can follow.

1.6.n: Marks the preceding action as the means of achieving what follows.

1.8.n: This is Apple's product name, used as the object of 立てて.

1.9.n: Marks the iPhone as the thing being propped up.

1.10.n: The て-form of 立てる connects positioning the phone upright with using it.

1.11.n: Combines with ことができます to say this use is possible.

1.12.n: Turns the preceding action into a noun-like phrase in the ability pattern ことができる.

1.13.n: Marks the action expressed with こと as what is possible.

1.14.n: The polite form of できる expresses the ability to use the phone this way.

1.15.n: Adds this capability to a list and signals that more benefits follow.

2.0.n: Introduces another feature in the explanation.

2.1.n: Points to the item being demonstrated; the object marker を is omitted in casual speech.

2.2.n: 回転する becomes 回転させる to express causing something to turn.

2.3.n: Turns 回転させる into a noun-like phrase before もできる.

2.4.n: Replaces が in ことができる to add another possible action.

2.5.n: The plain form expresses ability before the reason connector ので.

2.6.n: Presents rotation as the reason the following placement is possible.

3.0.n: Refers to placing the phone sideways, in landscape orientation.

3.1.n: Marks the sideways orientation in which the phone is placed.

3.2.n: Points to the placement being demonstrated and describes 感じ.

3.3.n: Together with こんな, it describes the demonstrated manner.

3.4.n: Marks こんな感じ as how the phone is placed.

3.5.n: 置いて is the て-form of 置く; です here is a spoken filler, not a standard verb ending.

3.6.n: With the preceding です, it creates a conversational pause while the speaker demonstrates.

3.8.n: This is the platform's name, used here for the videos watched on it.

3.9.n: Casually presents YouTube as one example, without implying criticism here.

3.10.n: This segment belongs to 見たり, formed from 見る to introduce an example activity.

3.11.n: In 見たりする, たり presents watching as an example rather than an exhaustive list.

3.12.n: Completes the たりする pattern for doing activities such as watching.

3.13.n: Links the described activity to こと, packaging it as another possible use.

3.14.n: Makes the preceding description into a noun-like phrase that can take も.

3.15.n: Adds watching videos this way to the other available uses.

3.16.n: The polite form of できる states that this activity is possible.

4.0.n: Introduces one more benefit of the stand.

4.1.n: Combines with 調整 to specify what can be adjusted.

4.2.n: Together with 角度, it names the ability to change the viewing angle.

4.3.n: Includes angle adjustment among the stand's useful features.

4.4.n: Points to the adjustment currently being demonstrated.

4.5.n: In こんな感じ, it describes the demonstrated manner of adjustment.

4.6.n: Marks the preceding phrase as the way adjustment can be performed.

4.7.n: Describes being able to adjust the angle freely, just as desired.

4.8.n: Connects 自由自在 to ので; this describing word requires な in this pattern.

4.9.n: Links flexible angle adjustment to the conclusion that the stand is convenient.

4.12.n: Describes the stand as useful and easy to use.

4.13.n: Connects 便利 to explanatory ん; this describing word requires な before it.

4.14.n: Short for の, it presents the assessment as an explanation based on the demonstrated features.

4.15.n: Makes the explanatory ending んです polite.

4.16.n: Adds emphasis to the speaker's assessment before the softer ね.

4.17.n: Invites agreement and softens the emphasis of よ.

0.lit: So, first, the first feature is the stand function, you see.
0.tip: Number + つ + 目 indicates order: 1つ目 means the first item.

1.lit: By pulling it out and using it like this, you can prop up the iPhone and use it, and—
1.tip: A plain verb followed by ことができます means you can do that action.

2.lit: Also, you can make this rotate too, so—
2.tip: 回転させる means making something rotate, rather than simply saying that it rotates.

3.lit: Placing it horizontally like this, you see, you can also do things such as watch YouTube.
3.tip: The pattern たりする presents an activity as an example; even one example can use this pattern.

4.lit: Also, angle adjustment is fully flexible like this, so it really is convenient, you know.
4.tip: ので connects a reason to its result; after 自由自在, it takes the form なので.
